title: SET_BIT, CLEAR_BIT and MODIFY_REG are not atomic
body:
In systems using RTOS, functions SET_BIT and CLEAR_BIT are not atomic.

Since many macros from LL and HAL level are using SET_BIT and CLEAR_BIT functions, What is general recommendation in systems with RTOS?
We have also noticed implementation of ATOMIC_SET_BIT, ATOMIC_CLEAR_BIT, etc.  What is their intention, since they are mostly used only for UART driver?

Best regards, 
Ivan Sojic

comments.author: TOUNSTM
comments.body:
Hello @IvanSojic,

First of all, please excuse this late reply.

1. SET_BIT and CLEAR_BIT macros are indeed not atomic
2. In case of RTOS usage, it is customer application responsibility to manage the protection of shared resources by the different threads (via mutex).
3. ATOMIC_SET_BIT and ATOMIC_CLEAR_BIT macros were introduced to handle the specific case where parallel processes in bare metal implementation may need to access the same register for interrupt control; this is the case of UART driver where you can run in parallel Rx & TX processes and all interrupts are being handle in CR1/CR3 registers causing side effects if accesses are not atomic.

I hope this answers your question. Please allow me to close this issue.

With regards,

title: Reusing active timer for HAL Tick skips generation of its IRQHandler
body:
**Describe the set-up**
```
STM32CubeIDE

Version: 1.9.0
Build: 12015_20220302_0855 (UTC)
```
which uses
```
STM32CubeMX - STM32 Device Configuration Tool

Version: 6.5.0-RC4
Build: 20220225-1913 (UTC)

Copyright (c) 2022 STMicroelectronics. All rights reserved
```

**Describe the bug**

Moving the SYS timebase to a timer that was previously configured for something elese, but then disabled will cause an invalid configuration where the timer IRQs are not generated.

**How To Reproduce**

Issue is exclusive to the STM32CubeIDE Device Configuration Tool / STM32CubeMX code generation.

It is reproducible with an empty project.

- start with a fresh project on F1 platform, for example STM32F103RG MCU

  ![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF1/assets/106665537/22d6c311-b1dc-4e50-8b72-195ddc4d1da2)

  ![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF1/assets/106665537/b6d6cfed-e1e5-4bee-bf5a-0ffec83954fb)

- generate code using defaults

- configure free timer (eg. TIM6, will be used for the rest of this example) for HAL timebase, generate code

  ![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF1/assets/106665537/a6cbdeac-bb20-4e41-b833-c039eff86cda)

- revert HAL back to systick, generate code

  ![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF1/assets/106665537/1def6ff7-c558-4f6d-89d7-ff37311fb269)

- manually configure the timer (TIM6), enable interrupts, generate code

  ![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF1/assets/106665537/e684e406-e037-430f-b1ee-e21ce08214d1)

  ![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF1/assets/106665537/10e9f62d-69ed-4568-bf57-1093bbf45bab)

  As it was previously used for HAL, the timer gets configured with an interrupt priority of 15 (**this is also a bug**)

  ![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF1/assets/106665537/3b605a13-63fc-4cdf-85ba-c87e6052e773)

- disable the timer (TIM6), reuse it for HAL timebase source again, generate code

  ![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF1/assets/106665537/fe4ce3b3-8fc8-4539-8075-63719f7704fd)

  ![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF1/assets/106665537/44e42515-2dc1-4f8a-ba5c-a3aa22b10af8)

  This will generate the `stm32f1x_hal_timebase_tim.c`, configured for the timer (TIM6), but its IRQ Handlers will get removed, causing the platform to hang in `Default_Handler` at start.

  Notably, the following configuration line will be missing
```
NVIC.TIM6_IRQn=true\:15\:0\:false\:false\:true\:false\:true\:true
```

  One can recover from this configuration by
  - reverting HAL to SysTick
  - closing the Device Configuration Tool and reopening it back again
  - configuring HAL to that timer
  
  Closing and reopening also seems to mitigate the interrupt priority assignment when manually configuring the timer, it will be configured as other devices (in a fresh project it should be 5).

I could not reproduce it with the above procedure, but such changes may also cause the change of `TICK_INT_PRIORITY`

**Additional context**

There are some other related bugs
- https://community.st.com/t5/stm32cubeide-mcus/value-of-tick-int-priority-default-value-changed/td-p/136027
- https://community.st.com/t5/stm32cubeide-mcus/tick-int-priority-affected-by-enabling-trace-outputs/m-p/588892/highlight/true#M20524

title: MMC DMA Reads/Writes Fail to Update DMA Direction
body:
In stm32f1xx_hal_mmc.c, `HAL_MMC_ReadBlocks_DMA `and `HAL_MMC_WriteBlocks_DMA`, the DMA direction is set in the DMA CCR register before starting the DMA transfer. However, this register cannot be updated without first disabling DMA (clearing the EN bit in the CCR register). This is not currently done in the driver and therefore the DMA direction is never updated between MMC reads and writes.
```
hmmc->hdmatx->Init.Direction = DMA_MEMORY_TO_PERIPH;
MODIFY_REG(hmmc->hdmatx->Instance->CCR, DMA_CCR_DIR, hmmc->hdmatx->Init.Direction); // Fails to set because EN bit is set
```

```
__HAL_DMA_DISABLE(hmmc->hdmatx);
hmmc->hdmatx->Init.Direction = DMA_MEMORY_TO_PERIPH;
MODIFY_REG(hmmc->hdmatx->Instance->CCR, DMA_CCR_DIR, hmmc->hdmatx->Init.Direction); // Works because EN bit was cleared above
```

This issue can be overcome by having the application code disable DMA (call `__HAL_DMA_DISABLE(hdma)` before calling either `HAL_MMC_WriteBlocks_DMA `or `HAL_MMC_ReadBlocks_DMA`. However, the driver should be fixed so this is not required.

title: Race condition in USB PCD control endpoint receive ISR
body:
**Describe the set-up**
Tested with STM32F103C8T6. Same code can be found for F0 series and others.

**Describe the bug**
Usually, the procedure to return control to the host after a handled SETUP packet in USB is done by receiving 0 byte on the OUT control endpoint. For PMA assisted chips this results in a) an interrupt which confirms the finished receive operation followed by b) an interrupt for the next SETUP packet. In case it takes quite long to handle the a) interrupt (due to low interrupt priority for example) the length information of the SETUP packet will be overwritten. This is the relevant part from the code:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF1/blob/6ead386a08dea17f4dffbdbcd36c9979cb53588b/Drivers/STM32F1xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f1xx_hal_pcd.c#L2130-L2174
The situation was already improved in 1.8.0 by avoiding the call of the user callback function in case of such an a) interrupt (see line 2157). However, the root issue remains and can lead to a race condition were a SETUP packet is received just between line 2152 and 2172 and the received byte count being overwritten in line 2172. This behavior can be proven by checking `(PCD_GET_ENDPOINT(hpcd->Instance, PCD_ENDP0) & USB_EP_SETUP) != 0` at line 2171.  
I suggest to properly re-check the `USB_EP_SETUP` bit and avoid `PCD_SET_EP_RX_CNT()` and `PCD_SET_EP_RX_STATUS()` if set.

Hi @STMAndreas,

First of all, we would like to thank you for your contribution.

The `TIM_RESET_CAPTUREPOLARITY` macro is used to reset an already set input capture polarity on a given channel which is the active edge of the input signal. The active edge can then be rising, falling or both depending on the TIM instance and the channel. 

```
#define  TIM_INPUTCHANNELPOLARITY_RISING      0x00000000U                       /*!< Polarity for TIx source */
#define  TIM_INPUTCHANNELPOLARITY_FALLING     TIM_CCER_CC1P                     /*!< Polarity for TIx source */
#define  TIM_INPUTCHANNELPOLARITY_BOTHEDGE    (TIM_CCER_CC1P | TIM_CCER_CC1NP)  /*!< Polarity for TIx source */
```

Indeed, the  `TIM_RESET_CAPTUREPOLARITY` macro has been updated within release v1.8.0. In fact, input capture polarity on channel 3 can be whether rising or falling and never both edges. That's why the `TIM_CCER_CC3NP` was removed.

The compilation error, has been already spotted and fixed internally but not yet published. The fix will be available in the next release.

Since the issue is already fixed, please allow me to close it. Thank you for your comprehension.

With regards,

title: stm32f1xx's HAL_DMA_PollForTransfer can't be used for polling
body:
The `HAL_DMA_PollForTransfer` function of stm32f1xx misleadingly always finishes the current DMA transfer on timeout, whether it is complete or not. This means that you can't actually poll for whether the transfer is done, because the act of calling `HAL_DMA_PollForTransfer` will finish it.

Even if this is the intended behavior, please at the very least mention it in the documentation of the function.

**Expected behavior**
`HAL_DMA_PollForTransfer` does not set state to `HAL_DMA_STATE_READY` on timeout.

title: Broken reset handler for SMT32F103xE?
body:
I think reset handler in `Drivers/CMSIS/Device/ST/STM32F1xx/Source/Templates/gcc/startup_stm32f103xe.s` might be missing code responsible for initializing stack pointer.
```
Reset_Handler:
  ldr sp, =_estack    /* <=== Missing? */

/* Copy the data segment initializers from flash to SRAM */
  movs r1, #0
  b LoopCopyDataInit
```
I created a project for STM32F103ZET6 in STM32CubeMX (apparently up-to-date) and right away I noticed `malloc()` failing for larger buffer sizes (like 1kB). I noticed that `_sbrk()` was failing because of stack collision check. Turned out that SP register was set to near beginning of SRAM block (something like `0x2000014a`, basically right after BSS section). After adding this one line to reset handler everything started working nicely.

Is this how it's supposed to work? I am totally new to all this, so feel free to ignore this report. I just thought I'd let you know of potential problem. Thanks!

comments.author: ALABSTM
comments.body:
Hi JimVonMoon,

I hope you are doing well. Please excuse the delay it took, but we finally got a feedback from our development teams.

Below are the details, hoping it answers your question:
* Stack pointer initialization
  The vector table contains the reset values of stack pointer and reset handler.
  After reset, the vector table is mapped at address 0, and the SP register is initialized with the same value as in the vector table.
  So technically there is no need to initialize the SP unless:
  * The Reset_Handler is explicitly called in the code.
  * The debugger is performing an emulated reset by setting the PC to the reset handler and forgetting about the SP default value.

  References:
  * http://infocenter.arm.com/help/index.jsp?topic=/com.arm.doc.dui0552a/BABIFJFG.html
  * http://infocenter.arm.com/help/index.jsp?topic=/com.arm.doc.dui0552a/Ciheijba.html

* Stack/Heap collision
  STM32F103ZE has 64K RAM. this means 0x2000014a as SP value is far from the end of RAM (0x20010000).
  Having a collision means either:
  * The user functions are using too much local variables.
  * The _estack value is wrong.

  An easy test could be to check the generated linked file (.ld) by CubeMX.

Please do not hesitate if you need more details or support. I let @tarek-bochkati answer you upcoming questions in the frame of this thread.

With regards,

It seems in my case it was a problem with the debugger. Everything seems to run fine without it, no need to set SP manually. Thank you for help!

comments.author: tgree
comments.body:
Actually, @ALABSTM that is not entirely correct.  The SP is *supposed* to be initialized based on the first interrupt vector entry.  However, in practice ST doesn't support that for all choices of address.  The ST boot loader validates the address first, and for some chips that have SRAMs aliased at both low (0x10000000) and high (0x20000000) addresses, the boot loader doesn't always support using the low addresses in the vector table.

See the following thread in community.st for more details of how I dealt with this and with how the __stack variable in the GCC startup script was very helpful in resolving the issue:

https://community.st.com/s/question/0D50X0000CEr55SSQR/bfb2-with-exception-vector-stack-in-ccm-sram
